facts.statement: Arenicolumba prattae was an extinct species of small pigeon that lived during the Miocene in Florida.
facts.quote: Arenicolumba prattae is an extinct species of small pigeon from the Miocene of Florida.

facts.statement: The species was described from a left coracoid fossil found at the Thomas Farm Site in Gilchrist County, northern Florida.
facts.quote: It was described from fossil material (a left coracoid) collected at the Thomas Farm Site in Gilchrist County, northern Florida, south-eastern United States.

facts.statement: The genus name Arenicolumba refers to the sandy, fossil-rich sediments of the discovery site, combining Latin words for 'sandy place' and 'pigeon'.
facts.quote: The genus name Arenicolumba comes from the Latin arena ("sandy place") with reference to the sandy, fossiliferous sediments of the collection site, and columba ("pigeon").

facts.statement: Originally described in 1992 as Columbina prattae, the species was reclassified into the new genus Arenicolumba in 2008.
facts.quote: Originally described in 1992 as Columbina prattae, it was moved to the new genus in 2008.

facts.statement: The species was originally classified under the genus Columbina before being moved to the genus Arenicolumba.
facts.quote: Originally described in 1992 as Columbina prattae, it was moved to the new genus in 2008.

facts.statement: Arenicolumba belongs to the bird family Columbidae.
Arenicolumba prattae lived during the Miocene epoch in Florida.
facts.quote: Arenicolumba prattae is an extinct species of small pigeon from the Miocene of Florida.
